channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula propõe levar jabuticaba para Trump: "Vou tentar levar uma para acalmá-lo"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he intends to gift Donald Trump a jabuticaba tree during a future trip, suggesting the fruit could have calming effects to help soothe the former U.S. president. The comment was made at the Embrapa-organized 'Brasil na Mesa' fair in Planaltina, following Lula’s return from an official trip to Europe. Lula also emphasized Brazil’s biodiversity potential and criticized the nation’s tendency to prioritize exports over its large domestic market.

item.title: Zema x Gilmar: cientista político aponta quem sai ganhando e perdendo com o embate
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema is using criticism of the Supreme Court as part of an electoral strategy to attract conservative and far-right voters, according to political scientist Leonardo Paz. Minister Gilmar Mendes’ judicial response may unintentionally amplify Zema’s visibility, creating ambiguous political effects. Paz warns that such institutional confrontations erode public trust and create opportunities for opportunistic politicians to exploit democratic fatigue.

item.title: Restrições da Lei Raul Jungmann não vigoram para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled that amendments introduced by the Raul Jungmann Law (Law No. 15.358/2026) to the Electoral Code cannot be applied to the 2026 elections, as they violate the principle of electoral annuality. The unanimous decision preserves voter registration and polling station setup in prison facilities, ensuring the changes will only take effect in future elections.

item.title: Empresas criticam e governistas elogiam avanço do fim da 6 X 1
item.description: The approval of the admissibility of the PEC proposing the end of the 6x1 work schedule (reducing the weekly workload to 40 hours) sparked criticism from business associations, warning of inflation risks, job losses, and reduced competitiveness, particularly in industrial sectors. Government supporters praised the move as fulfillment of a campaign promise by President Lula. The proposal now awaits the installation of a special committee by the Chamber's presidency to proceed.

item.title: Alerj pede que STF transfira governo interino do RJ para Douglas Ruas
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly (Alerj) asked the STF to transfer the state's interim government from Judge Ricardo Couto to the new Legislative President, Deputy Douglas Ruas (PL-RJ), arguing that his election on April 17 and inauguration on April 22 reopens the succession issue. The request is made in ADI 7942 (Justice Luiz Fux as rapporteur), while the injunction keeping Couto in office comes from Rcl 92644 (Justice Cristiano Zanin as rapporteur), whose joint judgment was suspended by a request for view from Justice Flávio Dino on April 9. Alerj claims the new legislative presidency constitutes a supervenient fact justifying a new deliberation, expressly reserved by the Court.

item.title: Gilmar defende inquérito das fake news até pelo menos as eleições
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes advocated for keeping the fake news investigation open at least until the 2026 elections, stating it remains necessary and that the Court is being vilipended. He referenced attacks by the rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI and forwarded a crime report to the PGR against presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema for allegedly dishonoring the Court in a social media series. The inquiry, launched in 2019, investigates criminal offenses against the Court and its members, with no set end date.

item.title: Moraes estende em 60 dias investigação sobre Monark por desobediência a ordem judicial
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes extended by 60 days the investigation into influencer Monark for repeatedly violating court orders to block his social media accounts and refrain from spreading false claims about electoral integrity. The Federal Police requested the extension, stating that Monark continued using platforms like Rumble, Spotify, and others to monetize antidemocratic content despite judicial blocks. The case is connected to the broader investigation into the January 8, 2023, attacks on Brazil’s government buildings.

item.title: TSE autoriza descentralização de recursos para Eleições 2026 no exterior
item.description: The TSE approved the decentralization of R$13.285.832,70 for the 2026 elections abroad, allowing the rental of properties outside Brazilian consular offices to set up 65 voting sections. The measure, requested by the MRE and TRE-DF, ensures voting rights for Brazilians overseas and complies with the Electoral Code’s minimum requirement of 30 registered voters per section.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia rejeita habeas corpus para manter Bolsonaro em prisão domiciliar
item.description: Supreme Federal Tribunal Minister Cármen Lúcia rejected a habeas corpus petition seeking to extend Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest beyond the initial 90-day period granted by Alexandre de Moraes. The ruling was based on the lack of authorization from Bolsonaro's official legal defense and the principle that habeas corpus does not apply against acts of a STF minister. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year and three-month sentence for leading an attempted coup, currently under house arrest for health reasons.

item.title: Brasil na Hannover Messe: entre o ufanismo e a entrega econômica
item.description: Brazil's participation in Hannover Messe 2026 featured announcements of approximately €2 billion in low-carbon hydrogen and derivative investments in Rio Grande do Norte, with President Lula da Silva and ApexBrasil leading the agenda to position the country in global green value chains. Despite the financial scale and symbolic weight, sector experts note that project realization hinges on regulatory frameworks, long-term financing, and stable demand, with many viewing the event as a platform for signaling intent rather than immediate contracts. ApexBrasil expresses optimism contingent on maturation timelines and highlights the Mercosul-EU agreement as a near-term catalyst, while cautioning against European tendencies to judge Brazil’s tropical agricultural model by their own standards.

item.title: Lula diz ter chamado delegados que estão 'fingindo trabalhar' para combater crime organizado
item.description: Lula said he asked the Justice Minister to recall Federal Police delegates and agents who are 'pretending to work' to combat organized crime, stressing that all positions should be filled by active servants. He also announced the hiring of 1,000 new federal police officers (630 agents, 160 clerks, 120 delegates, 69 experts, and 21 fingerprint specialists) by year-end. Additionally, he said he will bring jabuticaba to Donald Trump as a gesture to 'calm him down', amid ongoing tensions in Brazil-U.S. bilateral relations.

item.title: É #FAKE que governo Lula abriu comportas do rio São Francisco no Maranhão; vídeo foi gravado no Iêmen
item.description: The video claiming that the Lula government opened the São Francisco River’s floodgates in Maranhão in 2026 for electoral reasons is false. The footage was filmed in Yemen in March 2026, shows gate openings due to seasonal flooding, and contains Arabic audio with no Portuguese narration. The federal government denied the claim, stating no water release occurred for electoral motives.

item.title: Moraes abre prazo para PGR e defesa, e processo contra Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação a autoridades entra na reta final
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has granted a 15-day window for the Prosecutor General’s Office and Eduardo Bolsonaro’s defense to present final arguments in a case alleging coercion of authorities. Bolsonaro, who resides abroad and has twice waived his right to defend himself, is accused of orchestrating international sanctions — including export tariffs, visa suspensions, and Magnitsky Law applications — to pressure the STF ahead of his father’s trial. The Public Defender’s Office is representing him due to his failure to appoint counsel.

item.title: Gilmar desdenha Zema e diz que mineiro não sabe falar português
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes criticized presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) for his manner of speaking, stating he 'speaks a language close to Portuguese, but which is understood as offensive' in two interviews on the same day. Zema responded on social media, accusing Mendes of elitism and authoritarianism, arguing that the issue is not his speech but the actions of the minister and the STF that alienate power from the people.

item.title: Lula está certo: o campo progressista sucumbiu ao neoliberalismo
item.description: Maria Inês Nassif argues that Brazil's progressive field has succumbed to neoliberalism, validating Lula's critique that the left abandoned principles of social justice and national sovereignty in favor of fiscal adjustments and market alliances. She contends that this subordination weakened structural transformation capacity and left the country vulnerable to conservative setbacks.

item.title: Alerj pede ao STF que Douglas Ruas assuma o governo do Rio
item.description: The Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) filed a request with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) for state deputy Douglas Ruas, elected president of the House, to assume the state government. The argument is that Ruas’s effective inauguration as president of Alerj eliminates the justification for the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice (TJ-RJ) president, Judge Ricardo Couto, to continue acting as interim governor, a role he assumed due to a vacancy in the state’s constitutional succession line. The request was submitted to Minister Luiz Fux, rapporteur of the case concerning indirect elections in Rio, seeking an immediate and monocratic decision.

item.title: O que é a reciprocidade citada por Lula no caso Ramagem
item.description: President Lula praised the Federal Police's decision to revoke the credentials of a U.S. agent as a measure of reciprocity, in response to the expulsion of a Brazilian delegate operating in Miami linked to the Alexandre Ramage case. Reciprocity, while not a law, is a principle in international relations calling for proportional retaliation to actions by other states. Brazil enacted the Economic Reciprocity Law in April to allow countermeasures against unilateral decisions by other countries that impact national economy and sovereignty.

item.title: TSE mantém direito de preso provisório votar em 2026, mesmo após lei Antifacção
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled to maintain the voting rights of pretrial detainees in the 2026 elections, despite the new Anticorruption Law (Law 15.358/2026) that sought to prohibit voting for anyone imprisoned, regardless of final conviction. The Court determined the law cannot apply to the 2026 election due to the constitutional principle of annuality, which bars electoral law changes from taking effect within one year of an election. The ruling preserves current practices, including setting up polling stations in prisons and conducting voter registration for this population, which numbers around 200,000 individuals in Brazil.

item.title: Lula diz que dará maracujá e jabuticaba de presente para acalmar Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he plans to gift jabuticaba and maracujá to Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to calm them, emphasizing Brazil’s ability to grow these fruits anywhere. He also criticized Trump’s remarks about ending wars and advocated for UN Security Council reform to reduce global conflicts.

item.title: PL aciona TSE contra Lula por suposta propaganda eleitoral antecipada
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) filed a representation with the TSE against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, alleging premature electoral campaigning by using the Presidential Palace and official symbols in an April 14 interview to promote his re-election bid. The PL requested an urgent injunction to remove the interview videos from federal government and Lula’s personal social media accounts, ban the use of presidential infrastructure for electoral acts, and impose a financial penalty for violating Article 73 of the Election Law.

item.title: Declaração de Gilmar sobre inquérito até eleições provoca reação no Congresso
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes' defense of continuing the fake news investigation until the 2026 elections triggered an immediate reaction from opposition lawmakers, who criticized the use of the procedure during an election year. Deputy Carlos Jordy (PL-PB) was particularly vocal, questioning Mendes' impartiality and accusing the Supreme Court of acting with partisan bias.

item.title: Após Eduardo Bolsonaro faltar interrogatório, Moraes abre prazo para alegações finais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has opened the period for final arguments in the criminal case against Eduardo Bolsonaro, who is accused of coercion in the judicial process for attempting to pressure Brazilian authorities via the U.S. government to obstruct the investigation into the coup plot. Eduardo failed to attend a scheduled April 14 videoconference interrogation while residing in the U.S. with no set return date, and his defense is being handled by the Public Defender's Office due to his lack of private counsel. The Prosecutor General's Office has 15 days to respond, followed by the DPU, ahead of a potential trial in the First Chamber.

item.title: Febraban defende nome de Jorge Messias para o STF: 'Trajetória absolutamente compatível'
item.description: Three financial institutions - Febraban, CNseg, and FIN - issued a note supporting the nomination of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union, to the STF, emphasizing his career as a guarantee of legal security and institutional strengthening. The note underscores the Senate's essential role in approval and acknowledges that, despite delays due to political disagreements with Davi Alcolumbre, the climate has improved and Messias would have the necessary votes for approval.

item.title: Gilmar dobra aposta em ofensiva contra Zema, que busca se projetar na eleição
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes criticized former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema for his remarks about the Court, stating that Zema only governed due to temporary injunctions that exempted him from paying federal debt and is now seeking political gain through inflammatory rhetoric. Mendes defended Zema’s inclusion in the Fake News Inquiry and argued that while Zema’s language resembles Portuguese, it is perceived as offensive and institutionally inappropriate.

item.title: Não vejo como um católico pode apoiar a esquerda, diz possível vice de Flávio
item.description: Federal deputy Simone Marquetto (PP-SP), a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), plans a series of meetings with Catholic leaders over the next two months to strengthen her ties with that electorate. She stated that she does not see how a Catholic could support the left, reinforcing a discourse aligned with the conservative base. The initiative is part of preparations for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Gilmar sugere relação de Alessandro Vieira com o crime organizado; senador rebate
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes suggested Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) might be threatened or financed by organized crime for proposing the indictment of judges in a report from the Organized Crime CPI. Vieira rejected the claims as pathetic, stating his vote was based on technical analysis of proven facts. The conflict continues after the CPI's dissolution, with Mendes asking the PGR to investigate Vieira and Vieira requesting the case be archived.

item.title: Tanto Gilmar
item.description: Gilmar Mendes, the dean of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court (STF), is criticized for appearing detached from Brazilian realities, with suggestions he aligns more with international interests than national ones. His defense against legitimate critiques from Romeu Zema, governor of Minas Gerais, is seen as weak and out of touch with domestic concerns.

item.title: Tarcísio x Haddad: a próxima pesquisa Quaest sobre a disputa pelo governo de São Paulo
item.description: Quaest will release on Wednesday, April 29, 2026, a poll with 1,650 interviews on the São Paulo gubernatorial race, testing a first-round scenario with Tarcísio de Freitas, Fernando Haddad, Kim Kataguiri and Paulo Serra, plus projecting a potential runoff between Tarcísio and Haddad. The margin of error is two percentage points, and the survey will also update voting intentions for the Brazilian presidency.

item.title: Alerj pede ao STF que Douglas Ruas assuma governo do Rio interinamente até decisão sobre eleição direta ou indireta
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro State Legislative Assembly (Alerj) asked the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to recognize newly elected Assembly President Douglas Ruas as the interim governor, arguing that the president of the State Court of Justice’s interim role was only justified due to the absence of a constitutional successor. Alerj contends that with Ruas’s election, the constitutional line of succession must be immediately restored to prevent the entrenchment of an exceptional arrangement and the erosion of the state constitution.

item.title: Governo Lula oficializa Auxílio Gás do Povo como política pública
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva formalized the Auxílio Gás do Povo as a federal public policy through the Official Gazette of the Union on April 23, 2026, integrating it into the National Energy Policy. The initiative aims to combat energy poverty, ensure access to LPG for low-income families, promote clean cooking, and support a just and inclusive energy transition, with guidelines on supply, price, quality, safety, and prevention of misuse of public funds.

item.title: Vieira sai em defesa de Zema contra Gilmar
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) expressed full solidarity with former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) following criticism from Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes. Vieira stated that Mendes' remarks constitute an attempt to criminalize Zema for opinions expressed in satirical videos. The defense was made on Thursday, the 23rd, amid broader debates on freedom of expression and judicial conduct.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro ironiza incapacidade do STF de prender foragidos da trama golpista: ‘Ainda estamos aqui’
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro mocked the Supreme Court's failure to arrest fugitives from the January 8 coup plot, posting a photo with Alexandre Ramagem and Allan dos Santos in the U.S. under the caption 'still here'. Both were convicted for their roles in the coup attempt and fled to the U.S., where they are advocating for sanctions against Brazil. Eduardo himself faces a potential conviction for defaming Tabata Amaral, with his trial delayed after Justice André Mendonça requested additional review time.

item.title: Lula diz que jabuticaba acalma e menciona envio a Trump e Xi Jinping
item.description: President Lula said he plans to bring jabuticaba to international leaders, including Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, claiming the Brazilian fruit has a calming effect. The remark was made during an Embrapa event in Planaltina-DF, where he praised national agricultural production. Lula suggested the gesture could serve as a form of soft diplomacy and cultural outreach.

item.title: PL aciona TSE contra Lula por entrevistas no Planalto
item.description: The PL filed a representation with the TSE against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, accusing him of using the Planalto Palace and official symbols for premature electoral campaigning in an interview given on April 14, 2026. The party claims violation of electoral law (Article 73 of Law 9.504/97) through improper use of public assets, electoral speech referencing a 'fourth mandate' and attacks on opponents like Flávio Bolsonaro, and an imbalance in media exposure.

item.title: Lula fala em dar calmante para Trump e jabuticaba para Xi
item.description: President Lula said he intends to gift jabuticaba to Donald Trump to 'calm' him during international trips, citing Brazil's ability to cultivate the fruit and noting that Queen Silvia of Sweden keeps a plant in a greenhouse in Europe. He also said he will bring jabuticaba and passion fruit to other leaders, such as Xi Jinping, as symbols of Brazil's agricultural potential, emphasizing the country's 'extraordinary potential' that is often underutilized. The statement was made at the opening of the Brasil na Mesa fair in Planaltina (DF), during a visit to the Pomar da Ciência and the 53rd anniversary of Embrapa.

item.title: Ao atacar o português de Zema, Gilmar Mendes mostra-se como é
item.description: Gilmar Mendes criticized the Portuguese of Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema in a tone that revealed his patrimonialist stance, treating the governor's speech as private property to be controlled. The linguistically directed attack exposed an authoritarian view of power, where linguistic norms are used as instruments of domination, aligning with Weberian patrimonialism.

item.title: Após embate com Zema, Gilmar Mendes defende inquérito das fake news: 'Vai acabar quando terminar'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes defended the continuation of the fake news inquiry, stating it must proceed at least until the elections to shield the Court from attacks, after proposing to include former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema as a target. Opposition lawmakers are drafting a new impeachment request against Mendes, who replied that the inquiry 'will end when it ends'.

item.title: Pastor influenciador é investigado por suspeita de injúria homofóbica
item.description: Pastor Moisés Neri dos Santos, known as Pastor Moisés and with over 234 million social media followers, is under investigation for suspected homophobic injuria after making offensive remarks during a preaching at the Clériston Andrade General Hospital in Feira de Santana, BA. His defense claims the statements were based on biblical teachings and directed at the general public, not a specific individual, but the Bahia Civil Police opened the case, as homophobia is legally equivalent to racism in Brazil. He was questioned, released, and the case was formalized via a Termo Circunstanciado de Ocorrência (TCO).

item.title: Em Planaltina, Lula diz que vai levar jabuticaba para Trump para 'acalmá-lo'
item.description: At an Embrapa event in Planaltina, President Lula said he plans to bring a jabuticaba plant to Donald Trump to 'calm him down', highlighting Brazil’s fruit potential. He also emphasized the need to better utilize Brazil’s domestic market, comparing states like São Paolo to entire European countries. The remarks come amid diplomatic tensions between Brazil and the U.S. following the return of a Federal Police agent and reciprocal measures by both governments.

item.title: 46% estão mais preocupados com conta de luz do que com clima
item.description: Nearly half of Brazilians (46%) prioritize lowering electricity bills even if it increases pollution, while 77% are concerned about rising energy tariffs. Despite this, 70% view climate action as urgent and 71% believe Brazil should do more to combat climate change, though only 34% see the country as a global leader in this effort.

item.title: Hablla percorre Brasil e Uruguai com evento de WhatsApp e IA
item.description: Brazilian startup Hablla announces the Conversational Growth Experience 2026, a series of events across nine Brazilian cities and one in Uruguay, focused on practical WhatsApp Business and AI operations for commercial results. Officially supported by Meta, the events feature validated operational architecture, applicable metrics like Conversation Score and real-time SLA, and founder-led Q&A, targeting marketing, sales, and customer success leaders aiming to scale via WhatsApp without proportionally increasing headcount.

item.title: Justiça do Paraná volta a proibir Gleisi de postar que Deltan está inelegível até 2031
item.description: The Paraná Electoral Court barred Gleisi Hoffmann (PT) from posting that Deltan Dallagnol (Novo) is ineligible until 2031, under threat of a daily fine of R$1,000. The ruling follows her sharing a 2023 TSE certificate that her team claims proves his ineligibility. Dallagnol argues the post misleads voters and exceeds the bounds of political criticism.

item.title: Governo quer trocar relator da 6×1 na Câmara, mas Motta pretende manter Paulo Azi
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta intends to keep Paulo Azi as rapporteur of the PEC ending the 6×1 work scale in the special committee, despite government pressure to appoint a loyalist. Azi already secured bipartisan support in the CCJ, including praise from the PT, and is well-regarded by the Centrão. The executive seeks greater ownership of the popular, electorally salient measure, competing with the Chamber for credit ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Caiado diz que Jair Bolsonaro não soube governar e que gestão ruim abriu caminho para o PT
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized Jair Bolsonaro's administration, stating that his 2022 election loss and failure to produce a successor indicate poor governance, which, he argued, paved the way for the PT's return to power. Caiado refrained from directly attacking Flávio Bolsonaro, saying it is up to voters to judge his readiness, and rejected the notion that his candidacy is merely another anti-Lula voice, advocating for a high-level debate centered on his own qualifications.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes defende inquérito das fake news: ‘Vai acabar quando terminar'
item.description: Minister Gilmar Mendes defended keeping the fake news inquiry open at least until the 2026 elections, stating it remains necessary due to attacks on the Supreme Court. He referenced the Organized Crime CPI report calling for his indictment and that of other ministers, which was rejected by the committee, and said he requested Alexandre de Moraes include Romeu Zema in the inquiry for sharing a satirical video about STF ministers and Banco Master.

item.title: Caiado defende anistia ampla e idade mínima de 60 anos no STF
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a pre-candidate for president, advocated for a broad amnesty for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, criticized the STF for alleged excesses, and proposed a minimum age of 60 to serve as a Supreme Court justice, along with a distinguished jurist background. He also supported reducing the workweek from 6x1 to 5x2, saying it would advance due to popular pressure, though he avoided a direct stance, rhetorically asking who would vote against it. Caiado criticized Lula’s economic policies and advocated for a return to presidentialism with greater budgetary control.

item.title: STM autoriza coleta de dados em processo de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Superior Military Tribunal authorized the collection of military documents from former President Jair Bolsonaro, including his service record and disciplinary history, to support a potential expulsion from the Army over his conviction for attempting a coup. The move responds to a request by the Military Public Prosecutor's Office, which also seeks to strip the ranks of other reserve officers convicted by the STF, such as Augusto Heleno and Braga Netto. Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and 3 months in prison, which, under the Constitution, justifies the loss of military rank.

item.title: Crusoé: “O problema é os brasileiros não entenderem os seus atos”
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and 2026 presidential pre-candidate, rebutted criticisms from Gilmar Mendes about his manner of speaking, stating that the issue is Brazilians not understanding his actions. Mendes made the remarks in interviews with Record News and Jornal da Globo. Zema defended his communication style as direct and technical, rejecting the portrayal as careless.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula vai à abertura de feira na Embrapa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the opening of the Brasil na Mesa fair at Embrapa Cerrados in Planaltina (DF) on Thursday, April 23, 2026, at 10:30 a.m., to mark the 53rd anniversary of Embrapa. The event showcases Brazilian agricultural research technologies and products, with attendance by Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and ministers of Agriculture, Agrarian Development, Education, and others. The fair runs through Saturday, April 25, highlighting national agropecuniary innovations.

item.title: Resultado do avanço de Zema sobre o STF vai testar roupagem de moderado de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Romeu Zema's (Novo) escalation of criticism against the STF, particularly targeting Minister Gilmar Mendes, is being used to test his moderate image in the 2026 presidential race, as he seeks to gain traction amid Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) similar moderate stance. Despite lagging in polls, Zema has seen increased social media engagement and Google search interest, with his Polymarket betting odds rising from 1.4% to 6.3% in days, signaling growing attention—though still far behind Bolsonaro's 39.1% and Lula's 39%.
